A self-contained React Native design system that mirrors the public API of dds-react-native components with zero external dependencies.

## Overview

The standalone design system lives entirely in `src/design-system/`. It has **zero `@ddsrn/*` dependencies** — everything needed is either a React Native primitive or inlined code.

## Why standalone?

This design system exists to demonstrate that the **migration path** (bare RN -> Expo -> Web) is purely a tooling concern, not a component concern. The same component API works on all three targets without modification.

## API compatibility with dds-react-native

All components use the same prop names as their `@ddsrn/components` counterparts. Migrating back to the real library is a one-line import change per file:

```tsx
// Standalone
import { Heading } from './design-system/Heading';

// Real library
import { Heading } from '@ddsrn/components/Heading';
```

The prop API is identical.

## Components

| Component | File | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| [ThemeProvider & useTheme](/design-system/theme) | `theme/ThemeProvider.tsx` | Context provider + hook |
| [Heading](/design-system/heading) | `Heading.tsx` | Semantic heading with level and visual size |
| [BodyText](/design-system/body-text) | `BodyText.tsx` | Body copy with size and content style |
| [Button](/design-system/button) | `Button.tsx` | Interactive button with 4 variants |
| [TopBar](/design-system/top-bar) | `TopBar.tsx` | Navigation bar with title and slots |

## Tokens

All design values are defined in `src/design-system/theme/tokens.ts`:

- **Colours** — Tesco light brand palette (typography, interaction, border, background)
- **Typography** — font sizes (`size12` through `size64`), line heights, font weights
- **Spacing** — `none`, `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `xl`, `xxl`
- **Border radius** — `sm`, `md`, `lg`, `pill`

Body copy component with size and content style variants. API-compatible with @ddsrn/components/BodyText.

## Usage

```tsx
import { BodyText } from './design-system/BodyText';

<BodyText size="md">Short form body copy.</BodyText>

<BodyText size="sm" contentStyle="longForm">
  Long form body copy uses a taller line height for readability
  in paragraphs with multiple lines.
</BodyText>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `size` | `"xs" \| "sm" \| "md" \| "lg"` | `"md"` | Font size |
| `contentStyle` | `"shortForm" \| "longForm"` | `"shortForm"` | Line height — `longForm` is taller for multi-line paragraphs |
| `style` | `TextStyle` | — | Additional style overrides |

| `xs` | 12px | 16px | 20px |
| `sm` | 14px | 18px | 22px |
| `md` | 16px | 20px | 24px |
| `lg` | 20px | 24px | 28px |

Interactive button with 4 variants and inlined accessibility logic. API-compatible with @ddsrn/components/Button.

## Usage

```tsx
import { Button } from './design-system/Button';

// Primary (default)
<Button onPress={() => console.log('pressed')}>Tap me</Button>

// Secondary
<Button variant="secondary" onPress={handlePress}>Cancel</Button>

// Disabled
<Button disabled>Unavailable</Button>

// Small
<Button size="sm">Compact</Button>
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `variant` | `"primary" \| "secondary" \| "tertiary" \| "link"` | `"primary"` | Visual style |
| `size` | `"md" \| "sm"` | `"md"` | Size |
| `disabled` | `boolean` | `false` | Disables interaction, reduces opacity to 0.4 |
| `isFullWidth` | `boolean` | `false` | Stretches button to fill container width |
| `onPress` | `(event) => void` | — | Press handler |
| `onPressIn` | `(event) => void` | — | Press-in handler |
| `onPressOut` | `(event) => void` | — | Press-out handler |
| `leftIcon` | `ReactNode` | — | Icon before label |
| `rightIcon` | `ReactNode` | — | Icon after label |
| `accessibilityLabel` | `string` | Children text | Screen reader label |
| `accessibilityHint` | `string` | — | Screen reader hint |

## Variants

| Variant | Background | Text colour | Border |
|---------|-----------|-------------|--------|
| `primary` | `colorInteractiveDefault` (Tesco blue) | White | None |
| `secondary` | White | `colorInteractiveDefault` | 1px blue |
| `tertiary` | Transparent | `colorInteractiveDefault` | None |
| `link` | Transparent | `colorInteractiveDefault` | None + underline |

## Accessibility

The `useButton` logic (inlined from `@ddsrn/headless`) handles:
- `accessibilityRole="button"`
- `accessibilityState={{ disabled }}`
- Auto-derived `accessibilityLabel` from string children
- Dev warnings for icon-only buttons without `accessibilityLabel`

Navigation bar with title and left/right slots. Platform-aware title alignment. API-compatible with @ddsrn/components/TopBar.

## Usage

```tsx
import { TopBar } from './design-system/TopBar';

// Simple title
<TopBar title="My Screen" />

// With left/right slots
<TopBar
  title="Settings"
  left={<BackButton />}
  right={<SaveButton />}
/>

// No border
<TopBar title="Fullscreen" hasBorder={false} />
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `title` | `string` | — | Centre title text |
| `left` | `ReactNode` | — | Left slot — typically a back button |
| `right` | `ReactNode` | — | Right slot — typically an action button |
| `hasBorder` | `boolean` | `true` | Show 1px bottom border (`StyleSheet.hairlineWidth`) |
| `style` | `ViewStyle` | — | Container style overrides |

## Platform behaviour

| Platform | Title alignment | Min height |
|----------|----------------|------------|
| iOS | Centred | 44px |
| Android | Left-aligned | 56px |
| Web | Centred | 44px |

This matches the `dds-react-native` TopBar behaviour — iOS follows Apple HIG, Android follows Material Design.

## Accessibility

- Container: `accessibilityRole="none"` (not a landmark)
- Title text: `accessibilityRole="header"` (announced by screen readers as a heading)

A complete guide to migrating a React Native app with a standalone design system to Expo, Expo Web, and beyond.

## What this guide covers

This guide documents the migration path of the **DDS React Native Hello World** application through 5 phases — from a bare React Native baseline to a fully web-capable Expo app with automated screenshots and a documentation site.

The application was built with a **standalone design system** (`src/design-system/`) that mirrors the public API of `dds-react-native` components — with no external `@ddsrn/*` package dependencies. This makes the migration portable and demonstrable in isolation.

## Migration path

| Phase | What changes | Screen code changes |
|-------|-------------|-------------------|
| [Phase 1 — Bare React Native](/migration/phase-1-bare-rn) | Baseline: bare RN + standalone design system | — |
| [Phase 2 — Expo SDK](/migration/phase-2-expo) | 5 config files only | None |
| [Phase 3 — Expo Web](/migration/phase-3-expo-web) | 3 web deps added | None |
| [Phase 4 — Screenshots](/migration/phase-4-screenshots) | Playwright script added | None |
| [Phase 5 — Astro Docs](/migration/phase-5-astro-docs) | This docs site | None |

## Key principle

> `git diff phase-1/bare-rn phase-3/expo-web -- src/` outputs **0 lines**.

The screen component and the entire design system are never touched across the migration. Only build tooling and configuration changes.

## Repository structure

```
dds-rn-hello-world/
├── src/
│   ├── design-system/        # Standalone components (zero @ddsrn/* deps)
│   │   ├── theme/            # ThemeProvider, useTheme, tokens
│   │   ├── Heading.tsx
│   │   ├── BodyText.tsx
│   │   ├── Button.tsx
│   │   ├── TopBar.tsx
│   │   └── index.ts
│   └── HelloWorldScreen.tsx  # The demo screen (never changes)
├── App.tsx                   # Root: SafeAreaProvider + ThemeProvider
├── docs/                     # This Astro docs site
├── scripts/                  # Screenshot capture (Playwright)
├── screenshots/              # Generated PNGs (Phase 4+)
├── ios/ + android/           # Native projects
└── package.json              # Changes per phase
```

## Goal

Create a standalone bare React Native app at `/work/dds-rn-hello-world/` that:

- Uses the **exact same toolchain** as the `dds-react-native` Playground
- Implements its own design system (`src/design-system/`) with zero `@ddsrn/*` dependencies
- Serves as the **baseline** that all subsequent phases diff against

## What was built

### Standalone design system

All components live in `src/design-system/` — no external packages required beyond `react` and `react-native`:

| Component | API |
|-----------|-----|
| `ThemeProvider` | `brand`, `mode` — same props as DDS |
| `useTheme()` | Returns `{ theme }` — same shape as DDS |
| `Heading` | `headingLevel`, `visualSize` |
| `BodyText` | `size`, `contentStyle` |
| `Button` | `variant`, `size`, `disabled`, `onPress` |
| `TopBar` | `title`, `left`, `right`, `hasBorder` |

Tokens are inlined in `src/design-system/theme/tokens.ts` — Tesco light colour, typography and spacing values.

### HelloWorldScreen

```tsx
// src/HelloWorldScreen.tsx
import { Heading } from './design-system/Heading';
import { BodyText } from './design-system/BodyText';
import { Button } from './design-system/Button';
import { TopBar } from './design-system/TopBar';
import { tokens } from './design-system/theme/tokens';
```

This file **never changes** across all 5 phases.

## Toolchain (matches dds-react-native Playground exactly)

```json
{
  "react": "19.0.0",
  "react-native": "0.84.0",
  "scripts": {
    "start": "react-native start --port 4477",
    "ios":   "react-native run-ios --port 4477"
  }
}
```

**Babel:** `module:@react-native/babel-preset`

**Metro:** `@react-native/metro-config` with `disableHierarchicalLookup: true`, port 4477

**Entry:** `AppRegistry.registerComponent(appName, () => App)`

Only 3 runtime packages — the minimum possible for a React Native app with safe areas:

Enabling browser rendering via react-native-web. The app runs identically in iOS, Android, and a browser — with no screen code changes.

## Goal

Enable the Hello World screen to run **in a browser** via `react-native-web`, with no changes to `src/`.

## Dependencies added

```bash
npx expo install react-dom react-native-web @expo/metro-runtime
```

| Package | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `react-dom` | React's browser renderer |
| `react-native-web` | Maps RN primitives (`View`, `Text`, `Pressable`) to DOM elements |
| `@expo/metro-runtime` | Expo's Metro runtime shim for web |

## Version alignment

Both `react` and `react-dom` must be the exact same version. Expo 53 expects `19.0.0`:

```json
"react":     "19.0.0",
"react-dom": "19.0.0"
```

## `app.json` — web bundler

```json
{
  "expo": {
    "web": { "bundler": "metro" }
  }
}
```

Metro is used as the web bundler (not webpack), which is the Expo SDK 53 default.

## Running on web

```bash
expo start --web --port 4477
# Opens http://localhost:4477 in the browser
```

## DDS component web compatibility

All 5 standalone design-system components are web-compatible out of the box:

| Component | Web status | Reason |
|-----------|-----------|--------|
| `ThemeProvider` | Works | Pure React context |
| `useTheme` | Works | Pure React hook |
| `Heading` | Works | `Text` -> `<span>` via react-native-web |
| `BodyText` | Works | `Text` -> `<span>` |
| `Button` | Works | `Pressable` -> `<div>` with event handlers |
| `TopBar` | Works | `View` -> `<div>` |

No SVG, no reanimated, no gesture-handler — the standalone design system has zero native-only deps.

## Goal

- Documents all 5 migration phases with code diffs

- Is locally hostable and ready to deploy statically (GitHub Pages, Netlify, Vercel)

## Framework

| Tool | Version | Role |

| [Astro](https://astro.build) | 7.3.2 | Static site generator |
| [@astrojs/starlight](https://starlight.astro.build) | 0.42.0 | Docs theme with sidebar, search, dark mode |

## Structure

```
docs/
├── package.json            # Astro + Starlight dependencies
├── astro.config.mjs        # Starlight sidebar config
├── tsconfig.json           # Extends astro/tsconfigs/strict
└── src/
    ├── content.config.ts   # Starlight docsLoader + docsSchema
    ├── assets/
    │   └── screenshots/    # PNGs from Phase 4 (copied in Phase 5)
    └── content/
        └── docs/
            ├── migration/  # Migration phase guides
            └── design-system/ # Standalone component API docs
```

## Running the docs site

```bash
cd docs
npm install
npm run dev     # http://localhost:4321
npm run build   # outputs to dist/
npm run preview # preview the built site
```

## Adding the root-level script

From the project root you can also run:

```bash
npm run docs
```

which is equivalent to `cd docs && npm run dev`.
